summary: Weekly POC sync focused on triaging TTFT variance and planning a kernel handoff experiment. Identified burst pricing gap, agreed to run coalescing experiment across two seq-len buckets, and requested additional traces and prompts from the customer. Clarified security questions around KMS and VPC for pilot stage.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-09 14:30 UTC | Duration: ~54m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luca (Redwood SE), Sasha (Redwood SE), Jordan (PulseForge ML), Priya (PulseForge VP Eng), Diego (PulseForge Infra), Sam (PulseForge SRE).

[00:00] Maya: ok folks, thanks for joining. quick agenda — triage the ttft spikes from last week's run, decide kernel handoff plan, and next steps on traces and pricing. sound good?
[00:18] Priya: yeah sounds good, want to make sure we don't lose time on the burst behavior.
[00:28] Jordan: quick note — we saw big spikes around 1.2s for first token during microbursts, median was 220ms but tail terrible. sent the sample trace last night, but it's small.
[00:42] Luca: got that, we pulled the trace into our local harness. initial hypothesis is a combination of seq-len variance and suboptimal kernel selection in the fastpath. might be falling back to the generic matmul kernel when the KV cache isn't hot.
[01:02] Diego: is that the thing you called the KV cache? sometimes the infra team says cache doesn't persist across warmups.
[01:10] Sasha: yeah kv cache, but also streaming handshake — small tokens trigger different scheduling. we noticed too that if the request comes in with chunked streaming, the pre-alloc path picks a conservative kernel.
[01:26] Jordan: real quick, we run two request types — short prompts (<=120 tokens) and long doc completions (400-1k). most user traffic is short prompts.
[01:38] Maya: that's helpful — so we should prioritize ttft for the short bucket. Luca, can you summarize the kernels you want to try?
[01:46] Luca: sure. Two approaches: 1) coalesced path where we force selection of small-seqlen-optimized kernels and enable continuous batching for the short bucket, 2) hybrid — dedicated small-kernel pool for short requests and fallback to generalist kernels for long seq. The coalesce experiment is faster to iterate.
[02:08] Priya: curious on the tradeoff: do we see throughput penalty if we bias toward small kernels?
[02:15] Luca: slight throughput loss for long sequences when you keep more small-kernel instances around, but the unit cost per token for short requests goes down because we avoid fallback penalty. and latency tail improves.
[02:28] Sam: can you remind me what you mean by fallback penalty?
[02:31] Luca: yeah, fallback penalty — when runtime can't pick a specialized kernel due to sequence shape or memory layout, it uses a slow camera - uh, generic matmul path — slower and higher-latency variance.
[02:46] Jordan: (laughs) camera path. we got it.
[02:50] Maya: ok, practical experiment: Luca proposes we run two coalescing runs on PulseForge traces — seq-len buckets 1: <=128, 2: 129-512. run with and without kv cache seeding. compare ttft p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
[03:06] Diego: we can give you 48h of real traffic but need to scrub PII. should be fine though.
[03:12] Maya: great. Jordan, can you confirm who will own scrubbing?
[03:15] Jordan: I'll take it, should be done by friday.
[03:18] [04:02] Luca: note — for the coalesce experiment we'll also toggle our streaming handshake flag (called "fasthand" in the harness, internal name). When fasthand is enabled, we pre-allocate the streaming buffer and pick small kernels more aggressively. Might reduce first-token jitter.
[04:22] Priya: security question — at pilot stage, we need to ensure keys never leave our VPC and KMS controls. how does Redwood handle KMS?
[04:31] Sasha: we have options — hosted pilot with customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) and a private deployment tie-in. for POC we recommend BYOK with an HSM-backed KMS. we also have audit logs and SAML SSO.
[04:48] Priya: do you have SOC2 cert?
[04:50] Maya: yes, SOC2 Type II in 2026 — we can share the attestation and the security pack after this call.
[04:59] Diego: and network — do you support VPC peering or an egress firewall?
[05:03] Sasha: VPC peering is supported for private mode; for hosted we do private endpoints + VPC connector. we can run the POC in a private VPC if needed.
[05:12] Jordan: back to latency — one observation: the microbursts correlate with certain endpoints that call a vector-embedding step before generation. embedding step sometimes takes 80-120ms and delays the streaming start.
[05:28] Luca: interesting — in that case we need to factor in upstream latency in the handshake; we can offset the start-of-stream timer so kernel selection has better signals.
[05:36] Maya: ok so experiments: coalesced kernels + kv seeding + handshake offset. Luca — can you enumerate the runs and the metrics you'll report?
[05:45] Luca: yes — runs: baseline (current), coalesce A (<=128 bucket coalesced, kv off), coalesce B (<=128 with kv seeded), coalesce C (bucketed 129-512 coalesce), and hybrid run with a small-kernel pool. Metrics: TTFT p50/p95/p99, streaming jitter, token cost per request, abort/retry rates, and kernel fallback percentage. We'll also capture traces with per-request kernel decisions.
[06:04] Priya: timeline? when can we expect the results?
[06:08] Luca: if we get the 48h trace by Sunday, we can run experiments Mon-Wed and share preliminary on Thu. so 2027-09-15 for full write-up.
[06:19] Jordan: sounds good. Diego — will you enable read-only observability for Redwood?
[06:23] Diego: yes, we can create a token and firewall rule. I'll do that Monday.
[06:30] Maya: pricing — we noticed microburst requests cause cost spikes. we need to propose burst pricing or a reserved buffer. we have a standard burst policy but will tailor a proposal for PulseForge.
[06:41] Priya: we are also evaluating reserved capacity for predictable throughput but haven't decided on commit size. Can you send a model of cost vs reserved size?
[06:49] Maya: yes — I'll send a tiered proposal: no-reserve (on-demand + burst surcharge), 1x reserved (medium), 3x reserved (discounted), and a hybrid with burst credits.
[06:59] [08:10] Jordan: one more technical nit — we run prompts that include function calls and sometimes tools. Do those affect kernel choices?
[08:18] Luca: function calls per se don't change kernel selection until generation begins. but if your prompt includes tool outputs (longer tokens), that shifts token distribution and kernel pick. we can simulate that in the trace.
[08:31] Sam: any concerns about quantization? we use q4f16 on some workloads; does that change the path?
[08:38] Luca: quantization helps, but it requires compatible kernels. some of our small-kernel optimizations are quant-friendly, others need alternate code paths. we'll mark quantized runs in the experiment matrix.
[08:50] Priya: can you list the artifacts you'll send after the experiment?
[08:54] Maya: sure — experiment results spreadsheet, kernel decision logs, cost projection, and a short replayable harness with instructions.
[09:02] Jordan: good. for security docs, we'll need the SOC2 and the KMS integration guide.
[09:06] Maya: will share those after the call.
[09:09] [09:50] Luca: small aside — we also think that adaptive hedging (start with fast kernel, if no progress in X ms, switch to broad kernel) could help microburst tails. that is more engineering heavy but worth noting for long-term.
[09:59] Priya: put that on backlog.
[10:03] Maya: quick recap — agreed coalesce experiment across two seq-len buckets, we will get 48h scrubbed trace + 10 representative prompts, Redwood runs experiments early next week, share results 2027-09-15, Redwood to send pricing variants and security pack.
[10:20] Jordan: yeah and Diego will create read-only observability access.
[10:24] Maya: ok last thing — any other blockers?
[10:27] Jordan: none on our side. maybe confirm that BYOK can be used for the pilot.
[10:31] Sasha: yes BYOK supported, but for the hosted path we'll need a short onboarding checklist — will send.
[10:36] Priya: thanks all.
[10:39] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with the action items.

End of transcript. Notes: occasional mis-attributions and minor transcription errors (e.g., "camera path" for generic matmul). References: shared drive link (internal) - https://drive.redwood.example/pulseforge-pp-2027, experiment spreadsheet placeholder https://sheets.redwood.example/exp-pulseforge-2027.
